key_insight: A single high-resolution turbulent snapshot contains enough recurring spatial structure to train a super-resolution model that reconstructs unseen flow fields and fine-scale vortices.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a data-efficient path for turbulence modeling and simulation enhancement when high-resolution DNS/experimental data are scarce or expensive.
method: Train a WDSR network only on overlapping patches from one high-resolution 2D homogeneous isotropic turbulence realization.
Predict unresolved patches and stitch them back together using Hann-window-weighted overlap-add.
Benchmark against interpolation and WDSR models trained on full snapshots at x32 and x64 super-resolution factors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved recovery of vortical structures, high-wavenumber energy, and multiscale statistics on previously unseen flow fields at extreme under-resolution.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the degree of spatial redundancy in the flow and on careful patch assembly to avoid seam artifacts or bias from a single training realization.
paper_title: Extreme-Scale Super-Resolution of Homogeneous Turbulence from a Single Realization
